title: Ind AS 40 "Investment Property"
outcomes: Identify investment property and distinguish it from PPE and inventory.
Measure investment property at initial recognition.
Apply the cost model and the fair value disclosures.

meta.exam_tip: Ind AS 40 allows only the cost model — never book fair value gains, but always disclose fair value.

concepts.title: What counts as investment property
body: Investment property is land or a building (or part of one, or both) held by the owner or a lessee under a right-of-use asset to earn rentals, for capital appreciation, or both — not for use in production, supply or administration and not for sale in the normal course of trade.

Examples: land held for long-term appreciation; land whose future use is not yet decided; a building let under operating leases; a vacant building held to be let; property being built for future use as investment property.

Not investment property: property held for sale in ordinary business (inventory); owner-occupied property and property awaiting disposal from owner use (PPE); property let under a finance lease. Dual-use property is split if parts are separately saleable; otherwise it is investment property only if owner use is insignificant. Ancillary services are fine, but significant services (as in a hotel) make it owner-occupied.
concepts.analogy: Ask why the property is held: rent or appreciation means investment property; use or trade means something else.
concepts.work: A building let to a fellow subsidiary is investment property in standalone accounts but PPE in the group's.

concepts.title: Recognition and initial measurement
body: Recognise when future benefits are probable and cost is reliably measurable. This applies both to initial costs and later costs of adding to, replacing part of, or servicing it; day-to-day servicing is expensed.

Initial measurement is cost including transaction costs such as legal fees, property transfer taxes and other directly attributable costs. Start-up costs, initial operating losses before planned occupancy and abnormal waste are excluded.

Deferred payment: cost is the cash price equivalent, with the difference treated as interest. Exchanges: fair value unless commercial substance is absent or fair value cannot be reliably measured. A right-of-use asset held as investment property follows Ind AS 116 initially.
concepts.analogy: Initial cost works like PPE: price plus costs to get it ready.
concepts.work: Stamp duty and registration on a let building are capitalised.

concepts.title: Cost model and fair value disclosure
body: Ind AS 40 permits only the cost model after recognition: the asset is measured under the Ind AS 16 cost requirements (cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment), unless it meets held-for-sale criteria (Ind AS 105) or is a right-of-use asset (Ind AS 116).
Land is not depreciated; buildings are depreciated over their useful lives, with significant components depreciated separately.

Even though the cost model is used, the entity must disclose the fair value of investment property, the extent to which a qualified independent valuer was involved, and cases where fair value could not be reliably measured. Rental income, direct operating expenses and restrictions are also disclosed.
concepts.analogy: In India, the balance sheet shows cost; fair value appears only in the notes.
concepts.work: A building bought for 500 and now worth 640 stays at its depreciated cost.

concepts.title: Transfers and disposals
body: Transfers to or from investment property occur only when there is a change in use, supported by evidence — e.g. start of owner occupation (to PPE), start of development with a view to sale (to inventory), end of owner occupation (from PPE), or inception of an operating lease to another party (from inventory). A change in management intention alone is not evidence.
Under the cost model, transfers do not change the carrying amount or the cost for measurement or disclosure purposes.

Derecognise on disposal or when permanently withdrawn with no expected benefits. The gain or loss is net disposal proceeds less carrying amount, recognised in profit or loss. Compensation from third parties for impaired or lost property is recognised in profit or loss when receivable.
concepts.analogy: A transfer needs actual change in use, not just a board decision.
concepts.work: Moving staff into a let building moves it to PPE at the same carrying amount.

illustrations.title: An office tower held for rent
illustrations.q: Skyline Ltd. buys an office tower for ₹480 lakh plus ₹20 lakh of legal and registration costs, to let it to tenants. Land component is ₹100 lakh. The building has a 40-year life and nil residual value. Fair value after 3 years is ₹640 lakh, and the property is then sold for ₹620 lakh. Compute initial cost, annual depreciation, carrying amount at the end of year 3 and the gain on sale.

jobs.title: Reviewing a property portfolio
jobs.situation: A real estate group holds let buildings, land banks and projects under construction.
steps: Depreciate buildings under the cost model.
Document any change in use with evidence.
jobs.takeaway: Purpose drives classification; fair value drives disclosure, not measurement.

mcqs.q: Under Ind AS 40, investment property after initial recognition is measured using:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 40 removed the fair value option. In practice: fair value is disclosed.
mcqs.topic: Cost model and fair value disclosure

mcqs.q: Land held for an undecided future use is:
mcqs.explain: Treated as held for capital appreciation. In practice: classification may change when use is decided.

mcqs.q: A hotel operated by its owner is:
mcqs.explain: Significant services make it owner-occupied. In practice: a leased-out hotel may differ.

mcqs.q: A transfer from investment property to PPE requires:
options: Evidence of a change in use
mcqs.explain: Intention alone is not enough. In practice: start of owner occupation is evidence.

mcqs.q: Property being built for sale in the ordinary course of business is:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 2 applies. In practice: real estate developers hold such stock.

mcqs.q: Which cost is excluded from the initial cost of investment property?
mcqs.explain: Start-up and early losses are expensed. In practice: capitalise transaction costs only.

mcqs.q: Under the cost model, the fair value of investment property is:
mcqs.explain: Disclosure is mandatory. In practice: state the valuer's involvement.
mcqs.topic: Cost model and fair value disclosure

mcqs.q: A building let to a subsidiary is, in consolidated statements:
mcqs.explain: The group occupies it. In practice: reclassify on consolidation.

mistakes: Treating group lets as investment property in consolidated accounts.

summary: Subsequent: cost model only; disclose fair value.
Transfers need evidence of change in use.
Disposal gain: proceeds less carrying amount.
remember: Group lets are PPE in consolidated accounts.
traps: Recognising fair value increases in profit.

viva.model: Land or buildings held to earn rentals, for capital appreciation, or both, rather than for own use or sale in the ordinary course.

viva.q: Which measurement model applies under Ind AS 40?
viva.model: The cost model, applying Ind AS 16 requirements, with fair value disclosed in the notes.

viva.q: When can property be transferred to or from investment property?
viva.model: Only on a change in use evidenced by events such as starting owner occupation or beginning development for sale.
Portions are accounted for separately if they can be sold separately; otherwise it is investment property only when the owner-occupied part is insignificant.

viva.q: What is the gain on derecognition?
viva.model: Net disposal proceeds minus the carrying amount, taken to profit or loss.

cases.title: Harbour Estates Ltd.
cases.case: Harbour Estates Ltd. owns: a mall let to retailers (cost ₹900 lakh, land ₹300 lakh, life 50 years); a plot bought for future appreciation; and an apartment block under construction for sale. In year 4 it moves its head office into one floor of the mall that cannot be sold separately; the floor is 3% of the mall.

mcqs.q: Annual depreciation on the mall (₹ lakh):
mcqs.explain: (900 − 300) ÷ 50 = 12. In practice: land is never depreciated.
mcqs.topic: Cost model and fair value disclosure

mcqs.q: The apartment block under construction is:
options: Capital work in progress of IP
mcqs.explain: Being built for sale in ordinary business. In practice: Ind AS 2 applies.

mcqs.q: After the head office moves in, the mall is:
options: Still investment property, as own use is insignificant
mcqs.explain: Three percent use is insignificant and the floor is not separable. In practice: reassess if use grows.

mcqs.q: The plot held for appreciation is measured at:
options: Fair value through profit or loss
mcqs.explain: Cost model only. In practice: valuer's report supports disclosure.
mcqs.topic: Cost model and fair value disclosure
